@graph.name: FUMD-AI Training & Postprocessing Workflow
@graph.description: Trains and evaluates a BiLSTM + Bahdanau-attention model that forecasts a vehicle's serving cell 1-7 seconds ahead from the FUMD-AI preprocessing workflow's AI-ready labeled dataset (dataset_labeled_w<W>.csv), then postprocesses the results. Five Jupyter notebooks cover the pipeline: window the dataset and fit encoders/scaler (1), train the model (2), evaluate it on a held-out split plus optional cross-run generalization checks (3), aggregate and compare metrics across runs (4), and map handover/migration events spatially by type and destination cell (5). A local/interactive orchestrator notebook, run_pipeline.ipynb, chains Steps 1-5 via one set of top-level parameters and runs out of the box against a bundled example data slice (Step 5 is skipped automatically if EVENTS_CSV_PATH is left unset); Step 5 also stands on its own for a standalone run against any real preprocessing output. Steps 1-3 are GPU/Slurm workloads intended to run inside a pinned Singularity/Apptainer container (see requirements/train.txt and slurm/*.sbatch) via bare `jupyter execute` -- there is no papermill in the target execution image, so headless parameterization is done by src/fumd_training_workflow/notebook_runner.py, a small nbformat/nbclient-based replacement (see that module's docstring), or by hand-editing each notebook's own tagged parameters cell before Slurm submission. Steps 4-5 are local/no-GPU postprocessing steps. An earlier version of this workflow also included a real-measurement base-station-location-estimation step, refactored from estimacion_antenas.ipynb; it was dropped because no real RSRP measurement data exists in either connected project folder to validate or exercise it against -- see README.md's "Notes on the source notebooks" section. See README.md for the full step-by-step description, inputs/outputs, execution environment, and validation status. Unless otherwise indicated, source code is MIT-licensed and explanatory text/figures are CC BY 4.0; input datasets retain the licences stated in their own metadata/source records.

@graph.name: Local/interactive orchestrator: Steps 1-5 end to end
@graph.description: Chains Steps 1-4 (load & window -> train -> evaluate -> aggregate metrics) via src/fumd_training_workflow/notebook_runner.py, passing each step's output into the next from one set of top-level parameters, for local/interactive development. Step 5 (map migration events) is chained too when EVENTS_CSV_PATH is set (positions are reused from DATASET_PATH); leave it unset/empty to skip Step 5. Writes every intermediate/final file, plus an executed copy of each step notebook for provenance, under OUTPUT_DIR/executed/. Also submittable to Slurm as one job (slurm/run_pipeline.sbatch), or with Steps 1-3 run standalone via slurm/train_model.sbatch / slurm/evaluate_model.sbatch instead -- see README.md's "Execution environment" section for the tradeoff (see also this notebook's own markdown cell).

@graph.name: Step 1: Load & window dataset
@graph.description: Loads a dataset_labeled_w<W>.csv, guards/normalizes to one row per vehicle per second, fits label encoders for categorical columns (with a reserved 'unknown' code for values not seen at fit time), splits by whole vehicle into train/val (avoids sliding-window leakage across the split), builds sliding-window sequences excluding lead/leakage columns, and fits the feature scaler on the training split only (reused transform-only everywhere else). Runs on a GPU/Slurm node in the pinned container image (see requirements/train.txt).

@graph.name: Step 1b (optional, alternate to Step 1): Combine & window multiple datasets
@graph.description: Alternate entry point to Step 1: loads and concatenates two or more dataset_labeled_w<W>.csv runs into one training set, shifting each source file's veh_id by a distinct offset first so vehicles from different runs (each numbered independently from 0) can never collide, then encodes/splits/windows/scales identically to Step 1. Adds a source_dataset provenance column. Not chained by run_pipeline.ipynb -- run once, standalone, before Step 2, holding at least one run back from DATASET_PATHS for Step 3's CROSS_RUN_DATASET_PATHS generalization check.

@graph.name: Step 2: Train model
@graph.description: Builds the 2x bidirectional-LSTM encoder + per-forecast-step Bahdanau additive-attention autoregressive decoder (7 softmax heads, one per second-ahead forecast) and trains it on Step 1's windowed arrays with early stopping. Saves the trained model, training history, updated run manifest, and a training-curves plot. GPU/Slurm step; requires TensorFlow 2.14.0 (see requirements/train.txt).

@graph.name: Step 3: Evaluate model
@graph.description: Evaluates a trained run on its own held-out validation split (per-output precision/recall/F1/top-2 accuracy/confusion matrix, plus an accuracy breakdown for migration-warning-window rows vs steady-state rows), then optionally loops over other dataset_labeled_w<W>.csv paths for a cross-run generalization check, reusing the fitted encoders/scaler transform-only. Writes structured CSV+JSON metrics. GPU/Slurm step (model.predict benefits from a GPU, though nothing is trained here).

@graph.name: Step 4: Aggregate training metrics
@graph.description: Reads structured Step 3 metrics from one or more run directories (e.g. different hyperparameters or architecture variants), concatenates them into a long-format table, and produces per-output-step comparison plots (accuracy, top-2 accuracy, F1) and a summary table -- from structured data, not regex-scraped logs. Local/no-GPU step.

@graph.name: Step 5 (optional): Map migration events
@graph.description: Matches handover/migration events to vehicle positions by nearest time, groups destinations beyond the top K into 'Otras', and plots events by type and destination cell, optionally overlaid with real BS coordinates (a hand-curated dict, e.g. from your own BS-location analysis or operator/OSM data) and an OSM street-network background (from a GeoPackage, read with no extra dependency, or a .osm.pbf via pyrosm). Defaults chain onto this repository's own bundled example slice, so it is runnable out of the box. Local/no-GPU step; not chained by run_pipeline.ipynb.

@graph.name: Headless notebook parameter injection and execution
@graph.description: inject_parameters/run_step: a small nbformat/nbclient-based replacement for papermill, built specifically because this workflow's real execution environment invokes notebooks via bare `jupyter execute` (nbclient's CLI) with no parameter-injection tool available. Used by run_pipeline.ipynb; individual Slurm-submitted steps are parameterized by hand-editing each notebook's own tagged parameters cell instead.

Slurm submission script for Step 2 (train_model): requests a GPU node and runs `singularity exec --nv --pwd /workflow ... jupyter execute notebooks/step_2_train_model.ipynb` against the pinned execution image. Edit the notebook's own parameters cell before submitting -- there is no external parameter injection at this layer.
Slurm submission script for Step 3 (evaluate_model), same pattern as train_model.sbatch.

Slurm submission script for the full chain (Steps 1-5) as a single job: runs `singularity exec --nv --pwd /workflow ... jupyter execute run_pipeline.ipynb` against the pinned execution image, the same invocation as train_model.sbatch/evaluate_model.sbatch just against run_pipeline.ipynb instead of one step notebook. An alternative to submitting train_model.sbatch/evaluate_model.sbatch individually -- see README.md's "Execution environment" section for the tradeoff (one GPU allocation held for the whole run, including the CPU-only steps, vs. per-step control).
